meta.title: IshRize — Scheduling intelligence for institutions
meta.description: Import your timetables, detect clashes automatically, and track attendance in real time. Built for universities, designed for any organization.

hero.headline: One timetable. Every department. No clashes.
hero.subheadline: IshRize turns your institution's spreadsheet chaos into a live, clash-free timetable — imported from the files you already have, edited collaboratively in real time, with attendance built in.

problem.heading: Every institution is running on spreadsheets.
problem.pain1Desc: The timetable lives in an Excel file that only one person can safely touch. Everyone else works from stale copies.
problem.pain2Desc: Venue and lecturer conflicts are checked by eye — and discovered by students after the schedule is published.
problem.pain3Desc: Sign-in sheets and ad-hoc lists that never reconcile with the actual sessions on the timetable.
problem.pain4Desc: Moving one session means phone calls to every affected department — and hoping nobody misses the memo.

howItWorks.heading: From import to live in three steps.
howItWorks.step1Desc: Upload your existing Excel or PDF timetable. AI handles messy formats and scanned documents; you review every row before anything is committed.
howItWorks.step2Desc: Drag and drop the master timetable. Departments decompose slots into real sessions, and clash detection fires automatically as you work.
howItWorks.step3Desc: Lecturers open sessions, students scan QR codes, and attendance analytics update in real time.

features.heading: Scheduling intelligence for institutions.
features.intro: The engine underneath is built for the way institutions actually schedule — departments, shared venues, cross-listed cohorts, and all.
features.item1Desc: Excel, PDF, even scanned documents with OCR. A human review step before commit — no silent overwrites.
features.item2Desc: Real-time sync and drag-and-drop editing. Everyone sees changes instantly — no stale copies, no refresh.
features.item3Desc: Venue conflicts, lecturer overlaps, and cross-department cohort clashes — flagged as they happen, resolved in one click.
features.item4Desc: Surface free venues, open time slots, and unused rooms per term — before they become problems.
features.item5Desc: Teaching-load balance, course ownership, and lecturer management — self-service for departments, without routing through central admin.

engine.heading: Four engines doing the work.
engine.intro: IshRize is not a spreadsheet with a nicer interface. Each part of the scheduling problem is handled by a dedicated engine, and all of them run against the same live data.
engine.engine1Title: Reads the timetables you already have
engine.engine1Desc: A positional parser that rebuilds a timetable's grid from the coordinates of the text on the page, so dense multi-column university PDFs arrive as structured slots instead of scrambled lines.
engine.engine2Title: Knows what cannot happen at once
engine.engine2Desc: Venue double-bookings, lecturer overlaps and cohort collisions across departments, evaluated continuously as the timetable changes rather than in a check at the end.
engine.engine3Title: Finds the space you did not know you had
engine.engine3Desc: Free venues, open time slots and rooms sitting unused for a whole term, surfaced on demand and filtered by capacity and department.
engine.engine4Title: Keeps everyone on the same timetable
engine.engine4Desc: Every change broadcasts over a live socket. Two coordinators editing at once see each other's work immediately, with no refresh and no conflicting copies.
engine.nextIntro: Detection is solved. Generation is what we are building now, turning the timetable from something you assemble into something you describe.
engine.next1Desc: A graph-coloring and constraint-optimization solver that produces a complete, clash-free timetable across departments, venues and cohorts.
engine.next2Desc: Say that a lecturer cannot teach before 10am, or that a course needs a lab with 40 seats, and have it become a formal rule the solver enforces.
engine.next3Desc: Every placement comes with the reason it was made, so a coordinator can challenge the timetable instead of accepting it.

attendance.heading: Attendance that works the way your sessions do.
attendance.intro: Attendance is built on top of the timetable, not beside it — every session is tied to a scheduled slot, so records and reality never drift apart.
attendance.surfaces: Students check in from the mobile app. Lecturers and coordinators live in the web dashboard.
attendance.point1Desc: Rotating QR tokens validated server-side — fraud-resistant by design.
attendance.point2Desc: Student, lecturer, and admin roles with enrollment required before attendance can be marked.
attendance.point3Desc: Attendance percentages, session history, course-level breakdowns, and exportable reports.

caseStudy.heading: How UG Mathematics replaced spreadsheets with IshRize
caseStudy.sub: The University of Ghana's Department of Mathematics was the first to adopt IshRize for scheduling and attendance.
caseStudy.challengeBody: Before IshRize, the department managed timetables for 40+ courses across multiple lecture halls using a shared spreadsheet. Clashes were discovered the morning of lectures. Attendance was tracked by passing around a paper sign-in sheet — easy to forge, impossible to analyze.
caseStudy.solutionBody: IshRize replaced the spreadsheet with a constraint-aware scheduling engine. The coordinator imports courses, venues, and time slots, and the system generates a clash-free timetable in seconds. Lecturers start sessions from their phones. Students scan a rotating QR code to mark attendance — no paper, no proxies.
caseStudy.result1Desc: The constraint solver eliminates double-bookings before they happen.
caseStudy.result2Desc: Up from an estimated 60% when tracking was manual and inconsistent.
caseStudy.result3Desc: The coordinator no longer spends half a day resolving timetable conflicts.
caseStudy.result4Desc: Department heads see attendance trends across all courses on a single dashboard.
caseStudy.quoteBody: We used to find out about a room clash when two lecturers showed up at the same door. Now the system won't let it happen.
caseStudy.quoteOrg: University of Ghana, Department of Mathematics
